# Multiple testing correction: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, q-values, Holm, Bonferroni, e-BH

> Free Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate calculator and p-value adjustment. Paste a list of p-values (or a CSV with a p-value column) and get adjusted p-values and the number kept by Bonferroni, Šidák, Holm, Hochberg, Benjamini-Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli, the two-stage Benjamini-Krieger-Yekutieli procedure and Storey's q-values, with Storey's pi0 estimate and a p-value histogram; e-values are corrected with e-BH. Checked against statsmodels. Runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

Free and open source (MIT). Results are statistical estimates from the data you supply, not medical, legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/fdr-multiple-testing/)

## Use it from code

- `node cli.mjs pvalues.csv --column p_value --alpha 0.05 [--method bh|by|bky|storey|holm|hochberg|bonferroni|sidak] [--csv|--json]`
- `node cli.mjs --kind e evalues.csv --alpha 0.1` for e-BH
- `node platform/agents/tools.mjs call fdr-multiple-testing analyze --input '{"values":[0.001,0.02,0.3],"alpha":0.05}'`

## What it answers

- Which of my many tests still stand after correcting for multiple testing, at a chosen false discovery rate or family-wise error rate.
- Each test's adjusted p-value (and q-value) under each method, and how many each method keeps.
- What share of my tests look like true nulls (Storey's pi0), and whether the p-value histogram looks healthy.
